title: Слухи на кухне и ультиматум Насти  (Kitchen Rumors and Nastya's Ultimatum)

segments.t: At the guest's table, Louis gasps upon recognizing his own missing button in the dessert while Chef Barinov struggles to keep his temper in check. Back in the kitchen, Senya and Fedya gossip about Louis and the Chef, and Nastya orders Sasha to confess to Max immediately.
Сейчас я не знаю, как это...
То, что он тебе сказал, правда?
Этот усатый твоему даже стихи читает.
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
'A button. Louis.' In Russian, the idea of 'button' flows naturally into 'Louis' without extra filler words.
Сейчас я не знаю, как это...
'Right now I do not know how this...' Notice how Russian expresses 'any minute' and 'this' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Max answers right away.
'Forgive us, we will fix everything at once.' The grammar packs 'excuse me' and 'will fix' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Thank you, I can manage myself.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'thank you' and finishing on 'myself'.
То, что он тебе сказал, правда?
'Is what he told you really true?' Notice how Russian expresses 'then' and 'honestly' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Louis answers right away.
Этот усатый твоему даже стихи читает.
'That mustachioed guy even recites poetry to yours.' The meaning hinges on 'this' working together with 'to read' in spoken Russian.
'He is cheating on your Louis with a woman.' Notice how Russian expresses 'changes' and 'a woman' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Well, did you talk to Max yet?' Louis anchors the line on 'come on', while 'Max' completes the thought. Max answers right away.
'What are you waiting for?' Max addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'are waiting'.
'Go over there and tell him right now.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'go' before landing on 'to him'.
'That is none of your business.' The grammar packs 'yes' and 'matter' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Louis answers right away.
'I do not have any lemons left.' In Russian, the idea of 'yes' flows naturally into 'lemon' without extra filler words.
'Let us go to the walk-in cooler.' Max brings out the contrast between 'let's go' and 'refrigerator' in a few short words. Let's hear the full exchange one more time at natural speed.
